candidates.name: Ljubljana Castle
candidates.price: Entrance to the Castle Courtyard, Chapel and Gift shop is free, but there is a charge for access to the tower
candidates.content: The tower has magnificent views all over the city. You can also see the Sava River and Kamnik Alps in the distance. Included is a 3D Movie of the history of Ljubljana from a pre-historic settlement to Roman Empire to modern times

candidates.name: Museum of Modern Art
candidates.content: For those who prefer contemporary art, MG+ houses the national collection of 20th-century Slovene art (paintings, sculptures, prints, drawings, photography, video and electronic media collections), a collection of works from the f

candidates.name: National Gallery
candidates.price: Permanent Exhibitions Adults €8 Concessions €6. see website for others.
candidates.content: Definitely worth visiting if you care about art. It exhibits two important permanent collections that include works of some of the best and most renowned Slovenian (impressionist) painters (Jama, Grohar, Jakopic, Azbe). You can al

candidates.name: National Museum of Slovenia - Prešernova
candidates.price: Free admission each first Sunday of the month
candidates.hours: daily 10:00-18:00, Thu 10:00-20:00, closed on public holidays.
candidates.content: The oldest and the largest Slovene museum. It was founded in 1821. Existent museum building on the Museum street, was built in 1888 and was the first, building, assigned solely to culture in Slovenia. Today its stores a rich colle

candidates.name: MGLC International Centre of Graphic Arts
candidates.content: Specialised in art shows, often in collaboration with international institutions. Normally on nearby sites but MGLC Tivoli Mansion is closed for renovation.

candidates.name: Dragon Bridge
candidates.content: Completed in 1901, designed by Croatian Jurij Zainovich. It is guarded by four detailed dragon statues from the city's coat-of-arms. Look out for the dragon motif throughout the city. Be careful around the Dragon Bridge area, as i

candidates.name: Sts. Cyril and Methodius Church
candidates.content: An Orthodox Church has five domes with golden crosses at their top. It was built from 1932 to 1936, with interior frescos painted between 1986 and 1997.

candidates.name: Ljubljana Cathedral
candidates.content: St. Nicholas's Church (cerkev sv. Nikolaja) was built between 1701 and 1706 on a site dating back to 1262. The fine interior includes fresco painted by Giulio Quaglio between 1703 and 1723.

candidates.name: Slovenian Museum of Natural History
candidates.content: Features an almost complete skeleton of a 20,000 year old mammoth found near Kamnik in 1938, a 200-million-year old fossil fish skeleton found in Triglav National Park, and a new, 13-m skeleton of a fin whale. Also has a large min

candidates.name: City Museum of Ljubljana
candidates.content: City history and temporary exhibitions.

candidates.name: Ursuline Church of the Holy Trinity
candidates.content: A Baroque style church built between 1718 and 1726.

candidates.name: Franciscan Church of the Annunciation
candidates.content: Built between 1646 and 1660, with a later front facade and bell tower.

candidates.name: Triple Bridge
candidates.content: The central span is from 1842: it became a bottleneck so in the 1930s footbridges were added on each side, fanning out slightly. On the north bank these lead into Prešeren Square, adorned by the statue of the national poet France

candidates.name: Republic Square
candidates.content: Where crowds gathered as Slovenia announced its independence from the Yugoslav Federation in 1991. The square has significant importance for Slovene history, as it was a place of important public gatherings (and demonstrations) in

candidates.name: Congress Square
candidates.content: One of the central squares, built in 1821. In 1988 the first free mass demonstration was held here, which was the start of the Slovenian spring, leading to the declaration of Slovenia's independence in 1991.

candidates.name: Plečnik House
candidates.content: Devoted to great Slovenian architect Jože Plečnik, who lived in this building from 1921 to 1957. The house contains rooms with the artist’s valuable original furniture and personal objects, an archive of his sketches and plans and

candidates.name: National Museum of Contemporary History
candidates.content: Slovenia's 20th-century history museum gives you a real sense of the country's roller-coaster ride through regime after regime. Its immersive exhibits include a walk-through World War I trench. The last exhibit shows the events ar

candidates.name: Old Town
candidates.content: The old town has two squares, Mestni trg (City square) with the Robba fountain and the city hall behind it, and, further on, Gornji trg (Upper square). Well preserved medieval buildings now house local designer shops, and several

candidates.name: Tomb of National Heroes
candidates.content: a tomb and a monument for the national heroes of the World War II resistance struggle in Slovenia, created in 1949.

candidates.name: Nebotičnik
candidates.content: A 13 storey high-rise.built in 1931, designed by Vladimir Šubic, with a cafe & bar on the top floor.

candidates.name: Ljubljana Mosque
candidates.hours: For non-muslims - Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu and Sat between 10 and 11 a.m., Exterior is free for all
candidates.content: An intricate set of buildings, the first mosque in the country.

candidates.name: Museum of Architecture and Design
candidates.content: Hosts a permanent exhibition of Jože Plečnik's works.

candidates.name: Museum of Contemporary Art
candidates.content: Opened in 2011 in the former military barracks complex this is complementary museum to the MG+. Opening hours and prices same as +MG. Adult combined tickets available.

candidates.name: National Museum of Slovenia - Metelkova
candidates.content: In the new building of the National museum of Slovenia on the Metelkova Street, are exhibited collections of the applied art heritage of Slovenia. The permanent exhibition brings together objects of applied arts from the 14th cent

candidates.name: Railway Museum
candidates.price: Adults €8 Children, students, pensioners €4 group & family prices available
candidates.content: Covers all aspects of the railway, Great selection of steam locos.

candidates.name: University Botanic gardens Ljubljana
candidates.hours: Open daily, Apr–Jun 07–19, Jul–Aug 07–20, Sep–Oct 07–19, Nov–Mar 07–17. Tropical glasshouse has reduced hours: Daily 10:00–16:45
candidates.content: Ljubljana Botanic Garden is the oldest Slovene cultural, scientific and educational institution. It was founded in 1810, the time of the Illyrian Provinces, as a garden of native flora and a section of the Central School (École Ce

candidates.name: House of experiments
candidates.content: A hands-on science "playground" for kids.

candidates.name: Metelkova
candidates.content: A self-declared autonomous culture place to gather for alternative artists, many subcultures and youth. What used to be a military barracks is now full of underground artists, bars and nightclubs. Metelkova can get crowded on Frid

candidates.name: Cankarjev Dom
candidates.content: Enormous arts and convention centre with concerts and performances.

candidates.name: Slovenian Philharmonic Orchestra
candidates.content: Orchestra dating back to 1701.

candidates.name: Križanke Outdoor Theatre
candidates.content: used for summer festivals.

candidates.name: Ljubljana Summer Festival
candidates.content: Opera, ballet and theatre festival held in July and August.

candidates.name: Kinoteka
candidates.hours: Open daily, but closed on Sundays and in July and August
candidates.content: Ljubljana's charming film museum where they have at least two movies a day. The movies range from classics to cult movies, from trash and horror to artistic masterpieces. All movies are presented in the original audio language, an

candidates.name: Olimpija Ljubljana
candidates.content: They play soccer in PrvaLiga, the top tier. Their home ground (capacity 16,000) is off the ring road 2 km north of city centre.

candidates.name: Water City of Atlantis
candidates.content: A water park offering 14 pools, thermal baths, slides and saunas. Special section is dedicated for children.

candidates.name: Laguna Fun & Spa
candidates.content: Offers open-air pools during the day and themed parties at night.

candidates.name: HourAway
candidates.content: Houraway offers high-quality bike rentals, including e-bikes, road bikes, and gravel bikes, along with guided and self-guided cycling tours. Their expertly designed day and multi-day tours cater to all fitness levels, showcasing S

candidates.name: Hot Air Balloon Flights
candidates.content: These launch at sunrise for one-hour flights, weather permitting. The launch spot is chosen on the day so the wind carries you over the historic centre. The whole programme is about 4 hours so reckon on a very early start.

candidates.name: Kinodvor
candidates.content: This is a small and very cool cinema that shows mostly new movies that are not playing in the blockbuster movie complexes. It has also a lot of special events, a great cafe and movies for children (Sundays).

candidates.name: Arena Play & Party
candidates.content: A great place to spend an evening. Main features include bowling, pool, laser games and a state-of-the-art 3D XpanD cinema theatre.

candidates.name: Cineplexx
candidates.content: A Multiplex.

candidates.name: Metelkova mesto
candidates.content: It's a squat with 6 clubs, each with its own style of music and programme. Gala Hala is the biggest and the music is very diverse - from funk nights to hip-hop and indie to rap and strange fun music. It has also concerts and an ou

candidates.name: Lepa Žoga
candidates.content: Main sports cafe/bar with sports regalia along the wall and a good, mixed crowd on most nights. Shows international rugby, all sorts of football games (European, English, Italian and other leagues) and other live sports. Has the b

candidates.name: Vinoteka Movia
candidates.content: Anyone with any interest in wine should visit here. The cosy, candlelit wine bar comes with knowledgeable barmen who can recommend a wine based on your tastes. The wine glasses are huge, so it's hard to tell if they were being sti

candidates.name: Sir William's pub
candidates.content: Located in the Art Nouveau part of Ljubljana city centre, offers more than 120 beer varieties and a large choice of teas and wines. It is vibrant in the evenings, particularly when it hosts themed events and beer tastings, while d

candidates.name: Cafe Antico
candidates.content: Great ambiance - bare wooden floors, high tables and stools, and vaulted ceiling.

candidates.name: Sax Hostel & Sax pub
candidates.content: Really cool colourful spray-painted cafe/bar along the canal. The place also serves as a hostel.

candidates.name: Cutty Sark
candidates.content: Lively pub with raucous atmosphere. Usually has live music.

candidates.name: Od Žmavca sosed pa ud brata prjatu
candidates.alt: Žmavc's neighbor and my brother's pal aka Žmavc
candidates.content: Markets to the "creative urban type." Burgers, coffee and alcoholic drinks.

candidates.name: Pod Skalco
candidates.content: Popular student pub with an almost 150-year-long tradition, frequented almost exclusively by locals. Loud music.

candidates.name: Lajbah
candidates.content: Beer hall with outdoor area. Large choice of craft beers & mainly Asian food.

candidates.name: Tozd
candidates.content: Bar with coffee & craft beers

candidates.name: Tektonix Craft Brewery
candidates.content: Microbrewery & bar close to railway station. Brewery tours available.

candidates.name: Union Pub
candidates.content: Pub at the Union brewery. food available. This is the opposite of a micro brewery.

candidates.name: Gas Station
candidates.content: Popular quirky bar with a 1961 Chrysler Newport as part of the seating.

candidates.name: Cafe Capri
candidates.content: A cozy cafe in the very center of Ljubljana, just a few steps away from the famous Dragon Bridge, offers healthy, delicious and inexpensive breakfasts and brunches. All dishes here are made from scratch and prepared fresh. Full ba

candidates.name: Roza Slon
candidates.content: Restaurant/takeaway offering tasty & healthy Thai meals with a choice of beers & soft drinks. they are also at a few other locations in the city. Some vegan options.

candidates.name: Hot Horse
candidates.content: Horse-burger chain with four city outlets. Huge burgers and other dishes; you order and pay first at the machine.

candidates.name: Gostilna Sokol
candidates.content: Authentic Slovenian cuisine, with serving staff got up in traditional costume. So inevitably it's touristy, but good food in huge portions and very good value for money.

candidates.name: Odprta Kuhna
candidates.content: Odprta Kuhna means "open kitchen". It's a collection of food stalls on Pogačarjev trg, just south of Triple Bridge.

candidates.name: Nobel Burek
candidates.content: Open non-stop, so it's popular late at night. Different kinds of burek (a leafy dough pie filled with mince meat or cheese).

candidates.name: Klobasarna
candidates.content: Hole-in-the-wall fast food restaurant serving seasonal Slovenian soups with traditional sausages and bread. You order and pay first at the machine.

candidates.name: Govinda's
candidates.content: Self-service buffet with vegetarian and vegan Indian food, great value.

candidates.name: Restavracija Mandala
candidates.content: Vegan self-service restaurant. Food sold by weight.

candidates.name: Falafel
candidates.content: The name is a clue. They also offer mezze dishes.

candidates.name: Figovec
candidates.content: Popular place serving pony steaks, horse goulash, and traditional Slovenian food.

candidates.name: JB
candidates.content: Modern international fare, pricey by local standards, and mixed reviews on food quality.

candidates.name: Sunday flea market
candidates.content: Two dozen or so stalls selling overpriced knick-knacks. Postcards, €10. Tito and Disney memorabilia, broken Chinese-made curios, rusty military paraphernalia.

candidates.name: Central Market
candidates.content: The central, open-air market features a wide array of local produce (exact items vary depending on the season), as well as local cheeses, breads and meats in the adjacent building. If you're lucky, you may still find sellers who h

december.text: Ljubljana is a year-round destination but you need to dress for the Balkan climate. Summers are warm, with daytime highs of 30°C. There are often public events and festivals, with streets converted from traffic thoroughfares to event spaces, but afternoons can be humid with thunderstorms and downpours. Early summer and

Ljubljana is an excellent starting point for cycling adventures, offering options for all skill levels. For e-MTB enthusiasts, trails in Golovec, Rašica, and Polhograjsko hribovje provide lush forests and stunning views.
